sentences.text:
Honourable Sri Justice N.V.Shravan Kumar
 Writ Petition No.7330 of 2025
Order:
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondents.
With their consent, the writ petition is being taken up for disposal at the admission stage itself.

2. This writ petition has been filed seeking the following relief:-
"to declare the action of the respondents in acquiring our land in respective Door No.2-256/38/2 to an extent of 111.11 Sq yards, Door No.2-238/12 to an extent of 233.33 Sq Yards and Door No.2-253/9 to an extent of 166.66 Sq Yards, Situated at Battisawargaon Village, Mavala Mandal, Adilabad District, without initiating any land acquisition proceedings and without paying the compensation under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, as being illegal, arbitrary,
unconstitutional and violative of Article 21 and 300-A of the Constitution of India ."

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. Brief facts in this writ petition are that petitioners claims to be the absolute owners and possessors of respective Door No.2-256/38/2 to an extent of 111.11 Sq yards, Door No.2-238/12 to an extent of 233.33 Sq Yards and Door No.2-253/9 to an extent of 166.66 Sq Yards, Situated at Battisawargaon Village, Mavala Mandal, Adilabad District, having acquired the same in the year 2023, through registered sale deeds.

While things stood thus, on 03.03.2025, respondent authorities informed the petitioners that they are proposing to acquire the subject lands and informed the petitioners to handover the subject lands within a week.

Aggrieved by the same,
petitioners have filed the writ petition.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the respondent authorities without issuing any notice and without following due process of law are trying to dispossess the petitioners from the subject land and pray this Court to direct the respondent authorities not to interfere with the petitioners peaceful possession over the subject property, without following due procedure as contemplated under law.

5. Learned Government Pleader appearing for respondents submits that at present he has no instructions whether the subject land would be acquired or not and would fairly submits that the respondent authorities will follow due process of law before initiating action on the subject property.

6. Recording the above submissions and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case this writ petition is disposed of directing the respondent authorities to follow due process as contemplated under law before initiating action on the subject property.
